references.text: Peter asks whether the parable Jesus has just told—the parable about being ready and watching—is directed to the disciples or to everyone. The context for this question is Jesus' teaching in Luke 12:22-40 about not worrying and being prepared for the coming of the Son of Man.

Jesus answers Peter's question with the parable of the faithful and wise servant in Matthew 24:45-51, which is the parallel passage to what Jesus says next in Luke 12:42-46. This shows that the parable has special relevance for those who have been given leadership responsibilities.
Peter also asks Jesus to explain a parable in Matthew 15:15, which demonstrates Peter's role as the one who often speaks up and asks questions on behalf of the disciples.

In Matthew 19:27, Peter asks Jesus: "We have left everything and followed you. What then will we get?" – once again, Peter asks a question to clarify whether Jesus' words apply specifically to the disciples.

Jesus' answer to Peter's question follows in Luke 12:42-48, where he tells the parable of the faithful and wise steward. The answer suggests that the parable applies to everyone, but with special responsibility for those who have been entrusted with much.
In Mark 13:37, Jesus says: "What I say to you, I say to all: Watch!" This sheds light on the question Peter asks – Jesus' call to watchfulness applies to everyone, not just the disciples.
